GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
  
 LOK SABHA 
  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3500 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21.03.2025 
  
RASHTRIYA MAHILA KOSH 
  
3500. SHRI BALWANT BASWANT WANKHADE:  
           
 Will the Minister of Women and Child Development be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  the details of the loan schemes being run under the Rashtriya Mahila 
Kosh(RMK) along with the eligibility norms to avail such loans; 
(b)  the number of women belonging to Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes who 
have been benefitted from the RMK during each of the last three years and the 
current year, States/UT-wise; 
(c)  whether the Government has received complaints regarding overcharging of 
interest rate on loans under the RMK during the said period and if so, the details 
thereof along with action taken/being taken by the Government on such 
complaints; 
(d)  whether the Government proposes to restructure/amend the RMK, if so, the 
details thereof and the reasons therefor; and 
(e)  the details of the steps taken/being taken by the Government to extend the 
coverage of RMK across the country? 
  
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR) 
   
(a) to (e): Rashtriya Mahila Kosh (RMK) was a society, registered under the 
Societies Registration Act 1860 as an apex micro-finance organization established 
in 1993 under the aegis of the Ministry of Women & Child Development (MWCD).  
  
Based on the report on ‘rationalisation of autonomous bodies’, by the Department 
of Expenditure, a proposal of the Ministry to close down ‘Rashtriya Mahila Kosh 
(RMK)’ was approved by the Union Cabinet. The closure of the organisation has 
been notified in the Gazette o f India(Extraordinary) vide notification dated 
12.03.2024.

records.ls|LS18_S4_U_3501:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3501 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21.03.2025 
  
MAHILA SHAKTI KENDRAS 
  
3501. SHRI VISHNU DATT SHARMA: 
  
Will the Minister of Women and Child Development be pleased to state: 
  
(a)   whether the Government is implementing the Mahila Shakti Kendras (MSKs) to 
empower rural women, especially in the State of Madhya Pradesh and if so, the 
details thereof;  
(b)   whether the Government has established MSKs in the districts of Katni, Panna 
and the town of Khajuraho in the Khajuraho Parliamentary Constituency;  
(c)   if so, the details thereof along with the measures being taken to ensure the 
success of the said scheme; and  
(d)   if not, the reasons therefor? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR) 
  
  
(a) to (d): The Mahila Shakti Kendra (MSK) Scheme was approved in November, 2017 
as a centrally sponsored scheme to empower rural women through community 
participation.  A third party evaluation study of MSK scheme was conducted by NITI 
Aayog in 2020. Taking into account the findings of the evaluation and after consultation 
with States/ UTs and stakeholders, the scheme was discontinued with effect from 
01.04.2022. 
  
However, Ministry of Women and Child Development is implementing the Umbrella 
Scheme named as ‘Mission Shakti’ with effect from 01.04.2022 across the country 
including the State of Madhya Pradesh which aim at strengthening interventions for 
women safety, security and empowerment. The ‘Mission Shakti’ has two verticals 
‘Sambal’ for safety and security of women and ‘Samarthya’ for empowerment of 
women.  
  

 “Hub for Empowerment of Women (HEW)”, a component under Samarthya, sub -
scheme of ‘Mission Shakti’ is functioning as a Project Management Unit (PMU) for 
monitoring and supervisory unit of Mission Shakti Scheme.  
  
The HEW centres also engage in widespread outreach and awareness through 
organising awareness activities, camps, and campaigns to disseminate information 
related to women centric schemes, programmes, policies and legislations. 
  
The HEW are operational in the State of Madhya Pradesh at State level as well as 
District level including the districts of Katni, Panna and the districts falling within the 
Khajuraho Parliamentary Constituency.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3502
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21ST MARCH, 2025
HIV SELF-TESTING
3502: SHRI ANURAG SINGH THAKUR:
SHRI KHAGEN MURMU:
SMT. APARAJITASARANGI:
Will the MINISTER OF HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state :
(a) the manner in which the Government plans to integrate HIV Self-Testing (HIVST) into
the existing National AIDS and STD Control Programme (NACP) Phase-V;
(b) the steps taken/proposed to be taken by the Government to ensure that the Self-Testing
kits are affordable and accessible especially for marginalized and vulnerable populations;
(c) the role of public-private partnerships in expanding the reach of HIV self-testing; and
(d) whether there are any existing collaborations with private healthcare providers and NGOs
and if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (d): Under the National AIDS and STD Control Programme (NACP), a health care
provider performs HIV screening coupled with pre-test and post-test counselling. The
screened reactive cases undergo confirmatory testing for HIV with pre-test and post-test
counselling at Integrated Counselling and Testing Centres (ICTCs) through a stringent three
test algorithm to ensure that test results are accurate. Pre – test and post – test counselling is
an integral part of HIV testing under the NACP due to the stigma and discrimination
associated with HIV . Till date, the Drug Controller General of India has not issued
certificate/ license to any HIV self – testing kit for use in the country. There is no provision
to integrate HIV self-testing into the existing National AIDS and STD Control Programme
(NACP) Phase-V .

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF WOMEN & CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3503 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21.03.2025 
 MINIMUM WAGES TO AWW AND AWH 
†3503. SHRI AMRA RAM: 
Will the Minister of Women and Child Development be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  the number of the sanctioned posts along with the number of Anganwadi 
workers (AWWs) and Anganwadi Helpers (AWHs) working against the said 
posts indicating the honorarium being paid to them, State-wise; 
  
(b)  whether the Government proposes to make AWWs permanent, if so, the time -
frame fixed in this regard and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
  
(c)  whether the Government contemplates to fix minimum wages for AWWs, State-
wise, if so, the time by which it is likely to be provided and if not, the reasons 
therefor? 
  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR) 
  
(a) State/UT wise details of approved positions along with the number of Anganwadi 
workers (AWWs) and Anganwadi Helpers (AWHs) working against the said posts are 
placed at Annexure I .  AWWs and AWHs are “honorary workers” from the local 
community who voluntarily come forward to render their services in the area of child 
care and development to help the community for which they are paid honorarium. 
From 1st October, 2018, Government of India has enhanced the honorarium of AWWs 
at main-AWCs from Rs.3,000/- to Rs.4,500/- per month; AWWs at mini - AWCs from 
Rs.2,250/- to Rs.3,500/- per month; AWHs from Rs.1,500/ - to Rs.2,250/- per month; 
and introduced performance linked incentive of Rs.250/ - per month for AWHs and 
Rs.500/- to AWWs. In addition, States/UTs are al so paying additional monetary 
incentives/honorarium to these functionaries from their own resources which vary from 
State to State.  Details are placed at Annexure II.  
  

With a view to incentivize and encourage the Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) and 
Anganwadi Helpers (AWHs), various initiatives have been undertaken including the 
following: 
(i)  Promotion: Under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, promotional 
opportunities for Anganwadi Workers have been enhanced. 50% posts of Anganwadi 
Workers are to be filled by Anganwadi Helpers with 5 years of experience and 50% 
posts of Supervisors are to be filled by promotion of Anganwadi Workers with 5 years 
of experience subject to fulfilment of other criteria. 
(ii)  Social Security Insurance Schemes: Insurance benefits have been provided to 
Anganwadi Workers and Helpers under Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana 
(PMJJBY) for life cover worth Rs.2.00 lakh  (covers life risk, death due to any reason) 
in the age group of 18 to 50 years and under Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana 
for accidental cover of Rs.2.00 Lakh (accidental death and permanent full disability) 
/Rs.1.00 Lakh (partial but permanent disability) in the age group of 18-59 years.  
(iii)  State Governments and UT Administrations have been requested to encourage 
eligible AWWs and AWHs to get themselves enrolled under the Pradhan Mantri Shram 
Yogi Mandhan (PM -SYM) Pension Scheme, which is a voluntary and contributory 
pension scheme for  the unorganized sectors in the country to ensure old age 
protection.  
(iv) Retirement date: States and UTs have been requested to adopt a uniform 
retirement date i.e 30 th April of each year with respect to Anganwadi Workers and 
Helpers to ensure proper human resource planning. 
(v) It has been announced in the interim budget FY 2024 -25 to extend healthcare 
annual coverage of Rs. 5 Lakhs under Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya 
Yojana (AB-PMJAY) to all Anganwadi workers and helpers. 
Government has issued orders for upgradation of all mini-AWC to regular AWCs. This 
would add an Anganwadi Helper in these Mini Anganwadi Centres across the country 
to share the burden of Anganwadi Worker.  
Besides under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, IT systems through the 
Poshan Tracker App have been leveraged to reduce the workload which has digitized 
& automated nine physical registers out of eleven prepared and used by AWWs. 
  
(b) & (c) No such proposal is currently under consideration.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.3504 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21.03.2025 
  
WOMEN AND CHILD COUNSELLING CENTRES 
  
3504. SHRI MAGUNTA SREENIVASULU REDDY: 
SHRI PUTTA MAHESH KUMAR: 
  
 Will the Minister of Women and Child Development be pleased to state: 
                                                                              
(a)  whether the Government has undertaken any schemes/Programmes/ 
initiatives for the construction and development of Women and Child 
Counselling Centres across the country;  
(b)  if so, the details of such programmes/schemes/initiatives and the funds 
allocated/utilised for the same during the last five years, State-wise and district-
wise in Andhra Pradesh; 
(c)     the number of women and child counselling centres proposed, approved and 
presently functional across the country, State-wise and districts-wise including 
Prakasam and Eluru district in said State;  
(d)  the number of women and child specialist psychologists, therapists and 
psychiatrists' positions available along with those presently employed and 
vacancies in child counselling centres in the country, State -wise and district -
wise in the said State; and  
(e)   whether the Government has put forward any guidelines/manual regarding the 
functioning/maintenance of child counselling centres, if so, the details thereof? 
  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR) 
  
(a) to (c): The One Stop Centre (OSC) is a component of the Sambal vertical under 
Mission Shakti provides integrated support and assistance under one roof to women 
affected by violence and those in distress, both in private and public spaces. It also 

provides services like medical aid, legal aid and advice, temporary shelter, police 
assistance and psycho -social counselling to needy women. As the scheme is 
demand driven, the States and UTs are encouraged to set -up at least one OSC in 
each district and additional OSC(s) in those districts which have higher rate of crime 
against women or have bigger geographical area and in as pirational districts. As on 
date, 894 OSCs are approved and out of which, 802 OSCs are operational across 
the country either in own building or pre -existing government building or rented 
accommodation. The State wise approved and operational OSCs is at Annexure-I. 
The details of district -wise approved and operational OSCs in Andhra Pradesh 
including Prakasam and Eluru district is at Annexure-II. Details of State-wise funds 
released for the One Stop Centres (OSCs) during the last five years are at Annexure-
III. 
 
Further, the Ministry is implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme namely, 'Mission 
Vatsalya' through States/Union Territories to deliver various services for Children in 
Need of Care and Protection and Children in Conflict with Law. It includes both 
Institutional Care services and Non -Institutional Care services.   Institutional Care is 
provided through the Child Care Institutions, as a rehabilitative measure. The 
programmes and activities in Homes, inter-alia, include age-appropriate education, 
access to vocational training, recreation, health care, counselling etc.  Under the Non-
Institutional Care component, support is provided to the children through Adoption, 
Foster Care, After Care and Sponsorship. There i s provision of counsellor in the 
District Child Protection Unit and in the Child Care Institution also.  
 The Ministry of Women and Child Development in collaboration with National Institute 
of Mental Health & Neurosciences (NIMHANS), Bengaluru established Support, 
Advocacy & Mental Health Interventions for Children in Vulnerable Circumstances and 
Distress (S AMVAD), a national initiative & integrated resource for child protection, 
mental health, & psychosocial care, that provides training and capacity building and 
other forms of guidance and technical support, to child protection functionaries.  
(d) and (e): As per the Mission Shakti guidelines, the Central Government provides 
100% financial assistance to States/ UTs for appointment/hiring 13 manpower 
resources including 1 Psycho -social Counsellor at each OSC. The overall 
implementation of the OSC  scheme lies with the State Governments/UT 

Administrations. The Ministry has issued ‘Mission Shakti’ and ‘Mission Vatsalya’ 
guideline for implementation of women and child related schemes during 15th Finance 
Commission period 2021-22 to 2025-26.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3505
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 21ST MARCH 2025
AIIMS IN MADURAI
3505 THIRU DAYANIDHIMARAN:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the current status of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) project in
Madurai along with the expected timeline for its completion;
(b) the details of total budget allocated/utilized for the Madurai AIIMS Project;
(c) whether there are any delays in fund disbursement that are affecting the progress of
the project and if so, the details thereof;
(d) the main reasons for the delay in the Madurai AIIMS project and the manner in which
these are being addressed;
(e) whether there are contingency plans to avoid further delays in construction and
operationalisation of the said project and if so, the details thereof; and
(f) whether the Union Government has provided regular updates to the State
Government and the public about the progress of the Madurai AIIMS project and if
so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (c): Establishment of All India Institute of Medical Sciences(AIIMS) Madurai has been
approved under Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY) at a project cost of
Rs.2021.51 crore. Currently, 26% of Phase-I work has been completed. As per the Loan
Agreement signed with Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) target date of
completion of the project is October, 2026. As on date, Rs. 239.27 crore has been released
for construction of AIIMS Madurai. There is no delay in disbursement of funds for the project
activities.
(d) to (f) : The foundation stone of AIIMS Madurai was laid in 2019 , however the land for
the project was handed over by the State Government in 2020. It was decided to obtain

funding for the project through Japan International Cooperation Agency(JICA) and the Loan
Agreement was signed between Government of Japan and Government of India in March,
2021. The Project cost was also revised on account of inclusion of 150 bedded Infectious
Disease Block and some other additions. The progress of the project is being regularly
monitored at the level of the Institute and the Ministry. In addition, a Steering Committee has
been constituted under the Chairpersonship of Principal Secretary (Health), Government of
Tamil Nadu to monitor and facilitate smooth implementation of the project .

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3506 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21st March 2025 
 
“Export of Traditional Medicines and Health Products” 
 
3506. Dr. Sambit Patra: 
Will the Minister of Ayush be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the targets set by the Government under AYUSH Oushadhi Gunvatta Evam 
Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana and the achievements made thereunder during the last five 
years;  
(b) whether the Government has implemented any action plan to enhance the export of 
traditional medicines and healthcare products through Oushadhi Gunvatta Evam Uttpadan 
Samvardhan Yojana and if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has set any targets for export of traditional medicines and 
healthcare products through Oushadhi Gunvatta Evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana; 
(d) if so, the details of the targets set and achievements made thereunder during the last three 
years; 
(e) whether the Government has taken any measures for effective quality control, safety 
monitoring and surveillance of misleading advertisements of AYUSH medicines; and 
(f) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHAV) 
 
(a) In the year 2021, Ministry of Ayush  has implemented a Central Sector S cheme- Ayush 
Oushadhi Gunavatta E vam Uttpa dan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY), t he total Budget 

2 
 
allocation to this scheme is Rs. 122.00 C rores for five years. The components of AOGUSY 
scheme are as follows:  
1. Strengthening and up -gradation of Ayush Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories to 
achieve higher standards. 
2. Pharmacovigilance of ASU&H drugs including surveillance of misleading 
advertisements. 
3. Strengthening of Central and State regulatory frameworks including Technical Human 
Resource & Capacity Building programs for Ayush drugs. 
4. Support for development of standards and accreditation/certification of Ayush products & 
materials in collaboration with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Quality Control of 
India (QCI) and other relevant scientific institutions and industrial R&D centres.  
            The first component of the Scheme is Strengthening and up -gradation of Ayush 
Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories to achieve higher standards. This component is 
intended to increase the standards of Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani and Homoeopathy (ASU&H) 
Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories ( DTL) to World Health Organisation(WHO) - Good 
Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration 
Laboratories(NABL) levels, respectively. Till date, 20 ASU&H pharmacies and 12 ASU& H 
drug testing laboratories have been supported financially under this scheme. 
             The second component of the Scheme deals with Pharmacovigilance Program for 
ASU&H Drugs, working through a three -tier network of a National Ph armacovigilance Centre 
(NPvCC), 5 Intermediary Pharmacovigilance Centers (IPvCs) and 99 Peripheral 
Pharmacovigilance Centers (PPvCs) across the country. In this regard, during the last five years 
(till February 2025), a total of 35928 misleading advertisements related to Ayush drugs have 
been identified , which are reported to the respective State Regulatory Authorities for suitable 
action against the defaulter(s). Also, the program is regularly reporting Suspected  Adverse Drug 
Reactions for ASU&H drugs, wherein 1762 such suspected signals have been reported till date. 
Further, towards sensitizing various healthcare professional cohorts, 2324 awareness programs 
have been conducted with 213673 beneficiaries. 
        Under the third component of the S cheme- Strengthening of Central and State 
regulatory frameworks including Technical Human Resource & Capacity Building programs for 
Ayush drugs,  three training programmes have  been conducted for Ayush drug regulators, 

3 
 
industry personnel and other stake holders in the different zones of the country, which are South 
Zone, North-Eastern states and Central Zone, till date. 
 
(b) to (d)  The action plan implemented by the Government to enhance the export of traditional 
medicines and healthcare products through Ayush Oushadhi Gunvatta Evam Uttpadan 
Samvardhan Yojana(AOGUSY) is as  follows:- 
          The first component of the Scheme - Strengthening and up -gradation of Ayush 
Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories to achieve higher standards is intended to increase the 
standards of ASU&H Pharmacies and DTLs to WHO -GMP and NABL levels respectively . The 
funding pattern details are as follows- 
 
1.  The State Govt./U.T.’s ASU&H Pharmacies/State Govt. ASU&H Cooperatives, State Govt. 
ASU&H PSUs are funded up to Rs. 6.00 crore for strengthening infrastructure & technology 
up-gradation and meeting associated recurring costs for upgrading pharmacy in terms of 
technology used and quantum of production whereas, the Private ASU&H Pharmacies are 
supported with 50% of the project cost limited to Rs. 3.00 crore for equipment, machinery 
and scientific instruments to achieve higher standards of GMP (like WHO-GMP, cGMP, EU-
GMP) for obtaining WHO -GMP certification within 2 and 1/2 years from the date of first 
disbursement of Grant-in-Aid. 
2. The State /U.T. Govt ASU&H Drug Testing Laboratories , Government and Research  
Councils laboratories are funded  upto Rs. 3.00 crore for strengthening infrastructure & 
technology up -gradation to acquire NABL accreditation and meeting recurring costs of 
chemicals & reagents, consumables  and technical manpower whereas, the Private ASU&H 
Drug Testing Laboratories/in house Quality Control Lab of GMP certified ASU&H 
manufacturing units are supported with  50% of the project cost limited to Rs. 1.50 crore for 
acquiring scientific equipment and instruments for NABL accreditation, in order to follow 
NABL Guidelines & get accredited as ‘NABL’ in stipulated time-frame. 
 
    Till date, 20 ASU & H pharmacies and 12 ASU& H drug testing laboratories have been 
supported financially. Further, for release of Grand -in-aid All India Institute of Ayurveda, New 
Delhi, AIIA is designated as Central Nodal Agency. The details of Grant-in-Aid are annexed as 
Annexure-I.  

4 
 
(e) and (f)  Yes, the measures taken for effective quality control, safety monitoring and 
surveillance of misleading advertisements of Ayush medicines are as follows; 
1. As prescribed in Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940 and Rules made thereunder, enforcement of 
the legal provisions pertaining to Quality Control and issuance of drug license of Ayurveda, 
Siddha, Unani and Homoeopathy drugs, is vested with the State Drug Controllers/ State Licensing 
Authorities appointed by the concerned State/ Union Territory Gove rnment. Rule 158 -B in the 
Drugs Rules, 1945 provides the regulatory guidelines for issue of license to manufacture 
Ayurvedic, Siddha, Unani medicines and Rule 85 (A to I) in the Drug s Rules, 1945 provides the 
regulatory guidelines for issue of license to manufacture Homoeopathy medicines. It is mandatory 
for the manufacturers to adhere to the prescribed requirements for licensing of manufacturing 
units & medicines including proof of safety & effectiveness, compliance with the Good 
Manufacturing Practices (GMP) as per Schedule T & Schedule M -I of the Drugs Rules, 1945 and 
quality standards of drugs given in the respective pharmacopoeia. Drug Inspectors collect 
medicine samples regularly from industries and Markets and sent it to State Drug Testing 
Laboratory for quality testing and take further necessary action(s) on the basis of such tests 
reports as per Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940 and Rules made thereunder . 
2. Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy(PCIM&H) on behalf of 
Ministry of Ayush lays down the Formulary specifications and Pharmacopoeial Standards for 
ASU&H drugs, which serve as official compendia for ascertaining the Quality Control ( identity, 
purity and strength) of the ASU&H drugs, included herein, as per Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940 
and Rules 1945 and compliance to these quality standards are mandatory for manufacturing, sale 
and stock of ASU&H drugs in India. The quality parameters included in the Pharmacopoeias and 
Formularies of Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani & Homoeopathic (ASU&H) drugs prescribing 
mandatory regulatory standards have been identified to align the parameters prescribed by 
WHO/other major pharmacopoeias prevalent worldwide. Implementation of these 
pharmacopoeial standards ensures optimum quality standards in terms of identity, purity and 
strength of ASU&H drugs. 
3. The  Pharmacovigilance Program for ASU & H Drugs has been implemented under  Central 
Sector Scheme Ayush Oushadhi Gunavatta E vam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY) , 
which work through a three-tier network of a National Pharmacovigilance Centre (NPvCC), Five 
Intermediary Pharmacovigilance Centers (IPvCs) and 99 Peripheral Pharmacovigilance Centers 

5 
 
(PPvCs) established across the country. All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi under 
Ministry of Ayush is the National Pharmacovigilance Co -ordination Centre (NPvCC) for the 
implementation of the National Pharmacovigilance program for Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani & 
Homoeopathy drugs. These centres are mandated to monitor and report the misleading 
advertisements to the respective State Regulatory Authorities for suitable action 
against the defaulter(s). Under the Pharmacovigilance program, as of February 2025, a total of 
35928 misleading advertisements related to Ayush drugs have been identified.  Also, the program 
is regularly reporting Suspected Adverse Drug Reactions for ASU &H drugs, wherein 1762 such 
suspected signals have been reported till date. Further, towards sensitizing various healthcare 
professional cohorts, 2324 awareness programs have been conducted with 213673 beneficiaries.  
Details are annexed as Annexure II.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.3507 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21.03.2025 
EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN 
  
3507. SHRI ESWARASAMY K: 
  
 Will the Minister of Women and Child Development be pleased to state: 
(a)  the details of schemes for empowerment of women and development of 
children by Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs) in Tamil Nadu; 
(b)  whether Government has put in place any mechanism to monitor the work being 
done by NGOs; 
(c)  if so, the details thereof; 
(d)  the details of the beneficiaries of various schemes during the last two years and 
the current year, State-wise; and 
(e)  whether these schemes have helped in improving the standard of life of 
beneficiaries, if so, the details of the method of assessment and the results 
thereof?  
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR) 
  
(a) to (c) The Ministry of Women and Child Development releases funds directly to 
States/UTs under its various schemes and missions. It does not release any funds to 
any Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs). 
  
(d) The State -wise details of beneficiaries under the schemes of the Ministry during 
the last two years and the current year are at Annexure-I. 
  
(e) Yes Sir. 
  
Mission Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0 seeks to address the challenge of 
malnutrition through improved nutrition content and delivery. It is a Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme, where the responsibility of implementation lies with the 
States/UTs. The mission adop ts a strategic approach to reduce malnutrition and 

improve overall health and immunity. This includes activities such as community 
engagement, outreach, behaviour change initiatives, and advocacy. It emphasizes 
maternal nutrition, infant and young child feeding norms, and the treatment of Severe 
Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM), with additional 
focus on wellness through AYUSH practices. 
Supplementary Nutrition is provided to target groups following revised nutrition norms 
that prioritize diet diversity, ensuring a balanced intake of calories, proteins, healthy 
fats, and essential micronutrients. Fortified rice is supplied to Anganwadi Cen tres to 
address micronutrient deficiencies and combat anaemia. Additionally, millet -based 
meals are encouraged at least once a week for Hot Cooked Meals and Take Home 
Rations (THR). Under the Wheat Based Nutrition Programme (WBNP) and Scheme 
for Adolescent Girls (SAG), subsidized food grains such as wheat, fortified rice, and 
coarse grains are distributed to States/UTs through the Department of Food & Public 
Distribution. 
  
Mission Vatsalya scheme is implemented through the State/ UT Governments as per 
standards of care and protection to secure the best interest of child which is provided 
under The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (JJ Act, 2015) 
(as amended in 2021). 
  
Mission Shakti –  
  
(i) One Stop Centre (OSC) scheme is being implemented by the Government across 
the country including State of Tamil Nadu to provide integrated support and assistance 
under one roof to women affected by violence and those in distress both in private and 
public spaces. It also provides an integrated range of services including medical aid, 
legal aid and advice, temporary shelter, police assistance, psycho -social counselling 
to needy women.   
(ii) Women Helpline provides 24X7 emergency and non-emergency response through 
telephonic short-code 181 to women, by linking them with appropriate authorities such 
as Police, One Stop Centres, Hospitals, Legal Services Authorities etc. Additionally, it 
provides information about women welfare schemes and programs to all women.    
(iii) Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) scheme launched on 22nd January 2015, is a 
mindset change program, aims at valuing the girl child and preventing gender- biased 
sex-selective practices. BBBP is a centrally sponsored scheme under Sambal vertical 
of Mission Shakti with 100% funding by the Central Government across all the districts 
of the country. The scheme aims to work towards the protection and education of girl 
child through multi-sectoral interventions and encouraging greater spend on activities 
that have on ground impact, e.g., promotion of sports among girls, awareness about 
PC-PNDT Act etc.  
(iv) Nari Adalat is an initiative aimed at empowering women by ensuring justice and to 
offer services such as alternate dispute resolution, grievance redressal, counselling, 
evidence-based decision-making, pressure group tactics, negotiation, mediation, and 
reconciliation. 
(v) Ministry of Women and Child Development is implementing Pradhan Mantri Matru 
Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) across the country, including rural areas of the country 
w.e.f. 01.01.2017. The PMMVY is a Centrally Sponsored Maternity Benefit Scheme 

under which cash incentives of ₹5,000/ - is provided directly to the Bank/Post Office 
account of the beneficiary in Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode for first child. The 
eligible beneficiaries receive the remaining cash incentive, as per approved norms 
towards maternity benefit under Janani Suraksha Yojana after institutional delivery, so 
that on an average a woman gets ₹6,000/-. Cash incentive of ₹6,000/- is also provided 
under PMMVY to eligible beneficiaries for second child subject to the second child 
being a girl. 
  
(vi) Sakhi Niwas Scheme aims to promote availability of safe and conveniently located 
accommodation for working women in urban, semi-urban and also in rural areas where 
employment opportunity for women exists. Under the Scheme, financial assistance is 
provided for running of Sakhi Niwas in rented premises for working women and for 
those women who are under training for job. Provision of Day Care Centre for children 
of the residents of the Sakhi Niwas is an important aspect of the scheme. 
(vii) ‘Shakti Sadan Scheme’ is an Integrated Relief and Rehabilitation Home for women 
in distressful situations including trafficked women.   It aims at creating a safe and 
enabling environment for the women in such difficult situations, to enable them to 
overcome the adverse circumstances.  
 (viii) Ministry of Women and Child Development has introduced Palna sub -scheme 
under Mission Shakti for all States/UTs w.e.f. 01 April 2022, for providing day care 
facilities and protection to children. Palna is a Centrally sponsored scheme ensuring 
the participa tion of State/UT government for day -to-day monitoring and proper 
implementation of scheme.  
Anganwadi centres are the world's largest childcare institutions dedicated to providing 
essential care and support to children ensuring delivery of care facilities till the last 
mile. In a first of its kind approach, Ministry has extended the services of c hildcare 
through Anganwadi cum Crèche (AWCC). This will ensure whole day childcare 
support ensuring their well-being in a safe and secure environment. Anganwadi cum 
Crèche initiative aims to increase the women work force participation in the economy. 
The o bjective of Palna component is to provide quality creche facility in safe and 
secure environment for children (from ages 6 months – 6 years), nutritional support, 
health and cognitive development of children, growth monitoring, immunization, 
education etc

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3508
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21.03.2025
SPREAD OF GBS
3508. SMT. ANITA SUBHADARSHINI:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:-
(a) whether there is an increase in the number of patients affected by Guillain-Barre
Syndrome (GBS) in the country in recent months;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
(c) whether the Government has constituted any expert committee to find out the cause of
spread of GBS and if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether the Government has formulated any roadmap to check the spread of GBS in
future; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY
WELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) & (b): As on 12th March, 2025, a total of 229 cases (suspected and confirmed) of Guillain-
Barre-Syndrome (GBS) have been reported in the country only from Maharashtra State. The
incidence of GBS shows that the cases have been in declining trend in recent months.
(c) to (e): Central technical team was deployed on 24/01/2025 comprising experts from the
National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro
Sciences (NIMHANS) and National Institute of Virology (NIV), Pune on site to study the
pathogens and outbreak. Majority of cases have been reported from specific clusters in Pune,
with additional cases in Nanded. The study was focused on identifying the exact source of the
outbreak, with a thorough examination of water supply systems, sources of water, and other
relevant factors. The investigation indicated that the most likely precursor of GBS in this
population group is prior infections caused by Campylobacter.
To check and monitor the future spread of the disease surveillance mechanism has
been established under the Integrated Disease Surveillance Program (IDSP)/Integrated Health
Information Platform (IHIP) portal, which captures suspected cases. Steps taken by the
Government to prevent the spread of GBS is given in Annexure.

Annexure-I
ANNEXURE REFERRED TO IN REPLYTO PART(d) & (e) OF THE LOK
SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3508 REGARDING " SPREAD OF GBS”
Steps taken by the Government to prevent the spread of GBS;
 Strengthening sanitation and hygiene measures.
 Efforts are made to ensure an uninterrupted supply of treated and clean water.
 Water sources are examined for leaks and damages, and corrective measures
are taken.
 Nodal officer have been appointed in private hospitals and chlorination have
been done in wells.
 Tankers of clean water have been arranged.
 Have conducted massive Information, Education, and Communication (IEC)
campaigns to raise awareness at the community level,
 Designated isolation wards set-up in government hospitals and special
packages under PM-JAY scheme have been included for treatment of GBS.
 Have expanded testing for suspected cases and collaborated with local
authorities to contain the spread.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
  
 
LOK SABHA  
UN-STARRED QUESTION NO. 3509 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21.03.2025 
  
CHILD CARE INSTITUTIONS 
  
3509. Shri Haribhai Patel : 
          Shri Raju Bista : 
  
Will the Minister of Women and Child Development be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Government has recently increased support for Child Care 
Institutions (CCIs) under the Mission Vatsalya scheme and if so, the details of 
the support provided during FY 2023-24, State-wise;  
(b) whether there have been any enhancements in non -institutional care services 
for children in need of care and protection and if so, the number of children 
supported under these services;  
(c) whether the Government has established any new District Child Protection Units 
or Child Welfare Committees as part of Mission Vatsalya and if so, the details 
of these establishments State-wise;  
(d) whether there are any specific initiatives aimed at improving educational and 
vocational training opportunities for children in CCIs, if so, the details thereof;  
(e) whether the Government anticipates that these efforts will lead to improved 
outcomes for children in care and if so, the details thereof along with the manner 
in which it will be measured; and  
(f) the details of the support provided under Mission Vatsalya in the district of 
Darjeeling and Kalimpong since its inception?         
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR) 
  
(a): Ministry of Women and Child Development is implementing a Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme namely ‘Mission Vatsalya’, through the State/ UT Governments 
on predefined cost sharing basis between the Central and the State Governments to 
deliver services for children in difficult circumstances which includes institutional care 
and non -institutional care services. The Child Care Institutions (CCIs) established 
under the Mission Vatsalya scheme support, inter-alia, age-appropriate education, 
access to vocational t raining, recreation, health care, counselling etc.  State-
wise funds released under Mission Vatsalya Scheme during the year 2023 -24 and 
number of CCIs supported under the scheme during the year 2023 -24 is at 
Annexure-I. 
  

(b) : Non -Institutional Care support is provided by way of sponsorship, foster care 
and after care to children in need of care and protection. The number of children 
approved under Mission Vatsalya Scheme during the financial years 2022-23, 2023-
24 and 2024-25 is as under : 
  
Financial Year Number of approved children 
2022-23 62,675 
2023-24 1,21,861 
2024-25 1,70,895 
  
(c) : Section 106 of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 
provides that every State Government shall constitute a Child Protection Unit for 
every District, consisting of such officers and other employees as may be appointed 
by that Government, to take up matters relating to children with a view to ensure the 
implementation of this Act, including the establishment and maintenance of 
institutions under this Act, notification of competent authorities in relation to the 
children and their rehabilitation and co-ordination with various official and non-official 
agencies concerned and to discharge such other functions as may be prescribed.  
  
Further, Section 27 (i) of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 
provides that the State Government shall by notification in the Official Gazette 
constitute for every district, one or more Child Welfare Committees for exercising the 
powers and to discharge the duties conferred on such Committees in relation to 
children in need of care and protection under this Act and ensure that induction 
training and sensitisation of all members of the committee is provided within two 
months from the date of notification. 
  
Details of State -wise District Child Protection Units and Child Welfare Committees 
supported under Mission Vatsalya during FY 2023-24 are at Annexure-II. 
  
   
(d): The Child Care Institutions (CCIs) established under the Mission Vatsalya 
scheme support, inter-alia, age-appropriate education, access to vocational training, 
recreation, health care, counselling etc. 
  
(e): The improved outcome can be envisaged based on the statutory and service 
delivery structures created under Mission Vatsalya Scheme, utilization of funds, 
beneficiaries supported under the scheme, presence of structures at State and 
District level name ly, State Child Protection Society (SCPS), State Adoption 
Resource Agency (SARA), Child Welfare Committee (CWC), Juvenile Justice Board 
(JJB), District Child Protection Unit (DCPU) and Child Care Institution (CCI).  
  
(f): An amount of Rs.119.14 crore has been released under Mission Vatsalya Scheme 
to the State of West Bengal including the district of Darjeeling and Kalimpong during 
the financial years 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 (till date).

HEALTHCARE INFRASTRUCTURE IN KONASEEMA ANDHRA PRADESH
†3510. SHRI G M HARISH BALAYOGI:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the number and details of healthcare centres/hospitals operational in Konaseema
district in the State of Andhra Pradesh including Government, private and specialty hospitals,
especially their capacity and facilities available;
(b) the number and details of medical personnel currently available across all healthcare
centres/hospitals in Konaseema district, categorized health centre-wise, especially doctors
(specialists and general), nurses, paramedics and other staff;
(c) the details regarding the current vacant positions across all healthcare
centers/hospitals in Konaseema district including reasons for vacancies and steps being taken
to fill them, health centre-wise and position-wise;
(d) the doctor-patient and nurse-patient ratio in Konaseema along with the steps
undertaken to improve these ratios;
(e) the details regarding the availability of essential medical equipment, diagnostic
facilities and critical care units in Government hospitals in Konaseema district;
(f) whether the Government has any plan to strengthen healthcare infrastructure in
Konaseema district, if so, the details thereof; and
(g) the details regarding the availability and implementation of telemedicine and digital
healthcare services in Konaseema district?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY
WELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (c) : Health Dynamics of India (HDI) (Infrastructure & Human Resources), 2022-23 is
an annual publication, based on healthcare administrative data reported by States/UTs.
Details of Primary Health Centres (PHCs), Community Health Centres (CHCs), Sub-
District/Divisional Hospitals (SDHs), District Hospitals (DHs) and Medical Colleges (MC)
functioning in rural and urban areas of Andhra Pradesh including Konaseema district along

2
with status of health manpower may be seen at the following link of HDI 2022-23:
https://mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/Health%20Dynamics%20of%20India%20%28Infrastr
ucture%20%26%20Human%20Resources%29%202022-23_RE%20%281%29.pdf
Further, as informed by State Government, a total of 153 Private Hospitals are functioning in
the State of Andhra Pradesh.
Details of health manpower sanctioned, in-position and vacant in Konaseema district is as
follows:
S.No. Name of Post Sanctioned Existing Vacant
1. Community health Officer (CHOs) 23 18 5
2. Staff Nurse 138 126 12
3. Public Health Nurse (NT) 29 20 9
4. Pharmacist 46 42 4
5. Lab Technician 47 45 2
(d): As informed by State, the Doctor-Patient and Nurse-Patient ratio in Konaseema district are
1:21279 and 1:13173 respectively. The National Health Mission (NHM) provides support for
improvement in health infrastructure, availability of adequate human resources in health
facilities, to improve availability and accessibility to quality healthcare especially for the
under-served and marginalized groups in rural areas. The Ministry of Health and Family
Welfare provides technical and financial support to the States/UTs to strengthen the public
healthcare system, based on the proposals received in the form of Programme
Implementation Plans (PIPs) under NHM. The Government of India provides approval for
the proposals in the form of Record of Proceedings (RoPs) as per norms and available
resources.
The Government of India has taken number of initiatives in the form of incentives and
honorarium to the medical professionals for encouraging better service delivery in rural and
remote areas across the country, which include:
i. Hard Area Allowance to specialist doctors for serving in rural and remote areas so
that they find it attractive to serve in public health facilities in such areas.
ii. States are also allowed to offer negotiable salary to attract specialist including
flexibility in strategies such as “You Quote We Pay”.
iii. Non-monetary incentives such as preferential admission in postgraduate courses for
staff serving in difficult areas and improving accommodation arrangement in rural
areas have also been introduced under NHM.
iv. Multi-skilling of doctors is supported under NHM to overcome the shortage of
specialists such as Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care
(CEmONC) and Life Saving Anaesthesia Skills (LSAS).

3
(e) & (f) : This Ministry supports ‘Free Diagnostics Service Initiative’ programme under
NHM with the aim to provide accessible and affordable pathological and radiological
diagnostics services closer to the community, which in turn reduces the Out of Pocket
Expenditure (OOPE). Diagnostics services are provided free of cost at all levels of public
health facilities across the country including Konaseema district of Andhra Pradesh [14 tests
at SHCs, 63 at PHCs, 97 at CHCs, 111 test at SDH and 134 tests at District Hospitals].
XV-Finance Commission has recommended grants aggregating to Rs. 70,051 Crores over the
period of five years (2021-2026) through local government to strengthen the healthcare
system in various States including the Andhra Pradesh. A total amount of Rs 2601.32 crore
has been allocated under FC-XV health grant for the State of Andhra Pradesh for FY 2021-22
to FY 2025-26. Under the XV-FC Grants, 7 BPHUs (Block Public Health Units) have been
approved for Konaseema district for infrastructure strengthening.
(g): Digital interventions have been introduced for healthcare delivery, with eSanjeevani-
national telemedicine service playing a key role in enhancing remote healthcare access
through video consultations. E-Sanjeevani is implemented in two variants: eSanjeevani OPD,
which enables direct patient-to-doctor video consultations and eSanjeevani AB-AAM
(Ayushman Arogya Mandirs), which facilitates doctor-to-doctor teleconsultations, allowing
primary healthcare providers to seek expert opinions from specialists in higher-level hospitals.
As on 06.03.2025, in Konaseema district of Andhra Pradesh, 13,16,692 tele-consultations
have been conducted in eSanjeevani AAM through 42 Spoke cum Hub operational as Hub
and 455 Spokes served by a team of 514 Medical practitioners and health workers.

PROBLEM DUE TO SNAKE BITES
3511. SHRI RAMASAHAYAMRAGHURAM REDDY:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:-
(a) whether the Government is aware that snake bites are a big problem in the country and if
so, the details thereof;
(b) whether the Government is aware that Telangana has a particularly high number of snake
bite cases and if so, the details thereof;
(c) the steps taken by the Government to redress the problem in this regard;
(d) whether any funds have been allocated for the same and if so, the details thereof; and
(e) whether there has been any awareness campaign on poisonous snakes and if so, the details
thereof alongwith the funding provided in this regard?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY
WELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (c): The Government is aware of the snake bites problem. The States and UTs of India
are reporting the snakebite cases regularly on Integrated Disease Surveillance Program
(IDSP)/Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP) portal. Telangana reported 2479
snakebite incidents cases in 2024 on the IDSP/IHIP.
The Government of India has taken several steps to address the issue of snakebite. The
intiatives taken by the Government is at Annexure-I.
(d) & (e): The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare provides technical and financial support
to the States/UTs under the National Health Mission (NHM), based on the proposals received
in Program Implementation Plans (PIPs) from the States/UTs. The details of the PIP State/UT
wise may be seen at the following link:
https://nhm.gov.in/index1.php?lang=1&level=1&sublinkid=1377&lid=744
Various initiatives taken by the Government on awareness generation on snakebites is at
Annexure-II.
*****

ANNEXURE-I
ANNEXURE REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (a) TO (c) OF THE LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3511 REGARDING "PROBLEM DUE TO SNAKE BITES"
 The States/UTs are reporting snakebite cases and deaths on Integrated Disease
Surveillance Program (IDSP)-Integrated Health Information Portal (IHIP) on real
time basis.
 The Guidelines for prevention and control of Snakebite have been developed under
the National Action Plan for Prevention and Control of Snakebite Envenoming
(NAPSE) which may be accessed at https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/wp-
content/uploads/2024/07/NATIONAL-ACTION-PLAN-FOR-PREVENTION-AN
D-CONTROL-OF-SNAKEBITE-ENVENOMING-NAPSE.pdf)
 Snakebite related treatment is part of Health System Strengthening (HSS)
component of NHM. Support is provided to all States/UT for ensuring availability
of emergency medicines, equipment’s, transport mechanism related to snakebite
and other emergency conditions. To ensure the affordability and accessibility of
polyvalent Anti Snake Venom (ASV) at each level, ASV has been included under
the National and State Essential Drug List. The States/UTs gets funds for ASV
through National Free Drug Initiative under National Health Mission (NHM).
 To strengthen effective implementation of snakebite prevention and control
activities in the country, funds are being provided to states for the following:
 Training of health professionals on Snake bite management, emergency care,
control etc. at State and District level;
 Meetings for advocacy, inter-sectoral coordination etc.,
 Surveillance and monitoring
 Public Awareness through IEC
 Have provided capacity building to health care providers to equip doctors in all
public health facilities across the country with the necessary skills for the
emergency management of snakebite cases.

ANNEXURE-II
ANNEXURE REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (e) OF THE LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3511 REGARDING "PROBLEM DUE TO SNAKE
BITES"
 A Booklet on Snakebite Prevention and Control: Available in both Hindi and
English, this booklet provides comprehensive guidelines on snakebite prevention,
control, and initial first aid measures for snakebite victims.
 Posters on Do’s and Don’ts for Snakebites: Designed for use in the general
community, these posters are available in Hindi and English, offering practical
advice to minimize risks and ensure proper response to snakebites.
 A Video on Snakebite Awareness: Produced in 10 regional languages, this video
aims to educate diverse populations effectively about snakebite prevention, first
aid, and the importance of seeking timely medical attention.

ANALYSIS OF DIAGNOSTIC TECHNIQUES ACT
3513: DR. T SUMATHY ALIAS THAMIZHACHI THANGAPANDIAN:
COM. SELV ARAJV:
SHRI SUBBARAYANK:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
a) whether the Government is aware that 4.6 lakhs girls were missed at birth each year between
2013-2017 in the country and if so, the details thereof;
b) whether the Government is planning to undertake any analysis on how girls go missing at
birth despite the existence of the Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT)
Act, 1994;
c) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons thereof;
d) whether the attention of the Government has been drawn towards a statement made by the
President of Indian Medical Association (IMA) against PC-PNDT Act made to prevent female
foeticide saying that the prohibitions under this act need to be dispensed with owing to its massive
failure over 30 years; and
e) if so, the details thereof and the response of the Government thereto?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (e) The Government of India enacts the Pre-conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic
Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act, 1994 for awareness generation and advocacy
measures to build a positive environment for the girl child through gender-sensitive policies,
provisions and legislation. As per the latest Sample Registration Survey (SRS) report 2020,
the Sex Ratio at Birth (SRB) (female per 1000 male) stands at 907.
The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare undertakes regular review meetings, awareness
generation activities, sensitization and capacity building workshops as well as issues regular
advisories to strengthen the implementation of the PC & PNDT Act across the country.
As per information received from Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), 'Police' and 'Public
Order' are State subjects under the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India. The
responsibilities to maintain law and order, protection of life and property of the citizens

including women & children rest with the respective State Governments. The State
Governments are competent to deal with such offences under the extant provisions of laws.
However, Ministry of Home Affairs has been issuing advisories from time to time with a
view to support and supplement the efforts of States/UTs to effectively deal with crimes
against women and children, which are available at www.mha.gov.in. These advisories inter-
alia consist instructions for effective implementation of law with special emphasis on crime
against women and children.

 SHRI DHAIRYASHEEL SAMBHAJIRAO MANE
 SHRI CHAVAN RAVINDRA VASANTRAO
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state :-
(a) the details of major agreements signed during the visit of European  
Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to India recently; 
(b) whether India and European Union has signed or proposes to sign  
any Free Trade Agreement;
(c) if so, the details thereof and the salient features of the said trade  
agreement between the two partners;
(d) whether India and European Union has also signed an agreement  
on  security  and  defence  partnership,  artificial  intelligence  and  the 

2
inter operation ability of digital public infrastructure and if so, the  
details thereof; and
(e) the manner in which the said free trade agreement with European  
Union is likely to be helpful in realising the India's dream of achieving  
the status of developed nation or Viksit Bharat by 2047?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH)
(a  &  d)     At  the  invitation  of  Prime  Minister  Shri  Narendra  Modi,  
President of the European Commission, H.E. Ms. Ursula von der Leyen,  
accompanied by the European Union College of Commissioners, paid  
an official visit to India on 27-28 February 2025. This was the first ever  
visit of the EU College of Commissioners together to India. During the  
visit, Prime Minister held delegation level talks with President Ursula  
von der Leyen. The second ministerial meeting of the India – EU Trade  
and  Technology  Council  (TTC)  and  bilateral  ministerial  meetings  
between the European Commissioners and their Indian counterparts  
were also held during the visit. 

3
During the meetings, all areas of bilateral co-operation  as well as  
global and regional developments of mutual interests were discussed.  
These  included  trade  and  investment;  critical  and  emerging  
technologies including AI, Semiconductors and DPI; clean and green  
energy;  defence  and  security;  sustainable  infrastructure;  talent  
mobility;  skilling  and  people  to  people  ties.  No  Agreements  were  
signed during the visit. A Leaders’ statement and a Joint Statement on  
the Second Ministerial Meeting of the India-EU Trade and Technology  
Council were issued at the conclusion of the visit.
(b,  c  &  e)  India  and  European  Union  have  resumed  Free  Trade  
Agreement negotiations in June 2022. Ten Rounds of Negotiation have  
been  held  till  date.  The  last  Round  of  Negotiation  was  held  from  
10th-14th  March, 2025 at Brussels. The proposed FTA is aimed at  
strengthening trade and investment linkages between India and the  
EU and support supply chain resilience through enhanced economic  
cooperation.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-3516
ANSWERED ON- 21/03/2025
CHARGES FOR DEPORTATION OF INDIANS
3516 SHRI MANISH TEWARI 
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:-
(a) whether the Union Government has paid any charges per person  
as deportation costs for Indian nationals recently deported by the  
United States, if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether  due  process  under  U.S.  immigration  law,  during  
expedited removal proceedings, was followed for these deported  
Indian nationals, if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether  the  Government  has  raised  any  concerns  with  U.S.  
authorities regarding Indian deportees being handcuffed, shackled  
and treated in a manner that undermines their basic human dignity  
and rights, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)  whether  Prime  Minister  Narendra  Modi  has  raised  this  issue 
during  his  recent  discussions  with  President  Donald  Trump  in  

2
Washington  D.C.,  if  so,  the  details  of  the  discussions  and  any  
assurances received thereon?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH)
(a) No. 
(b  to  d)  Since  January  2025,  the  U.S.  Department  of  Homeland  
Security’s Customs and Border Protection (CBP) vertical has been  
carrying out deportation operations as part of the larger “National  
Security initiative” led by the U.S. White House – National Security  
Council  (NSC).  The  individuals  that  have  been  deported  in  this  
operation were placed under “expedited removal” process, wherein  
a determination of inadmissibility can be made by the immigration  
officer without having to go through an immigration judge in the U.S. 
The Ministry of External Affairs remains engaged with the U.S. side  
regarding the humane treatment of  deportees during deportation  
operations. The Ministry has strongly registered its concerns with  
the U.S. authorities on the treatment meted out to deportees on the  
flight that landed on February 5th, particularly with respect to use  
of shackles, especially on women. 
It  may  be  noted  that  the  U.S.  Standard  Operating  Procedure  to 
organize and execute deportations effective from November 2012  

3
calls for the use of  restraints on deportees. The U.S. authorities  
have conveyed that restraints are applied to ensure the safety and  
security of the deportation mission. While women and minors are  
generally not shackled, the flight officer in charge of a deportation  
flight has the final say on the matter. The U.S. side has confirmed  
that  no  women  or  children  were  restrained  on  the  deportation  
flights that landed in India on February 15th and 16th respectively.  
This  has  been  confirmed  and  recorded  by  our  agencies  after  
interviewing the deportees on their arrival in India.  
The  need  to  promote  safe,  orderly  and  legal  migration  while  
cracking  down  on  illegal  immigration  networks  was  discussed  
during  the  recent  visit  of  Prime  Minister  to  the  U.S.  on  12-13  
February 2025. India’s consistent stance against illegal immigration  
while seeking humane treatment of deportees was reiterated. Both  
sides acknowledged the need to cooperate closely in aggressively  
addressing  illegal  immigration  and  human  trafficking  by  taking  
strong action against bad actors, criminal facilitators, and illegal  
immigration networks.

(a) the total amount of funds sanctioned and released under the Conservation, Development and 
Sustainable Management of Medicinal Plants Scheme till date, State/UT-wise; 
(b) the total number of projects funded by the said scheme till date, State/UT-wise especially in the 
State of Andhra Pradesh; 
(c) the details regarding the projects completed, ongoing projects and the timeline required for their 
completion along with the funds released till date; 
(d) the details of the total number of farmers trained under the projects supported for information, 
Education and Communication (IEC) activities of the said scheme, classified, State/UT-wise; 
(e) whether the Government has any data regarding the funds sanctioned and released under the 
component of Quality Testing and Certification of raw material of the said scheme; and  
(f) if so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise and funds released till date in this regard? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (I/C) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHAV) 
 
(a)  National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB), Ministry of Ayush, Government of India is 
implementing Central Sector Scheme on “Conservation, Development and Sustainable Management 
of Medicinal Plants” throughout the country including Andhra Pradesh wherein follo wing activities 
are supported:  

2 
 
(i) Information, Education & Communication (IEC) activities like Training / Workshops / 
Seminars/ Conferences etc. to promote the medicinal plants. 
(ii) Establishment of nurseries. 
(iii) In-situ conservation / Ex-situ conservation. 
(iv) Livelihood linkages with Joint Forest Management Committees (JFMCs) / Panchayats / 
Van Panchayats / Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs) / Self Help Groups 
(SHGs). 
(v) Research & Development. 
(vi) Promotion, marketing and trade of medicinal plants produce.  
(vii) Forward and backward linkage in supply chain of medicinal plants (Integrated 
Component) under which the following activities are supported: 
• Infrastructure for Quality Planting Material to raise the planting material of medicinal 
plants for cultivation.  
• Information Education Communication (IEC) activities to aware the farmers. 
• Infrastructure for Post -Harvest Management and Marketing to increase the 
marketability of the medicinal plants, adding value to the produce, increasing 
profitability and reducing losses. 
• Quality Testing and Certification of raw material. 
This Scheme has been approved for continuation for a period of five years from 2021 -22 to 
2025-26.  Grant-in-Aid sanctioned / released during  2021-22 to 2024-25 under Central Sector Scheme

AYUSHMAN BHARAT DIGITALMISSION (ABDM)
3519. SMT MAHIMA KUMARI MEWAR:
Will the Minister of HEALTH and FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the progress made under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) in
financial year 2024-25 in terms of Health ID generation, Health Professional Registry (HPR),
and Health Facility Registry (HFR);
(b) the number of healthcare facilities and professionals registered under ABDM in the
financial year 2024-25 across the country, State/UT-wise;
(c) the total financial incentives disbursed under the Digital Health Incentive Scheme (DHIS)
to encourage hospitals and clinics to adopt digital health solutions;
(d) the number of beneficiaries registered and vaccine doses recorded under the U-WIN
Portal since its launch; and
(e) the measures being taken by the Government to ensure interoperability, data security, and
privacy in India's digital healthcare ecosystem?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (e) As on 17.03.2025, a total 17,30,67,913 ABHA earlier known as Health ID have been
created, 2,73,055 health care professional have been registered on health professional registry
(HPR) and 1,49,257 healthcare facilities have been registered on health facility registry in the
financial Year2024- 25.
The state/UT wise number of verified registrations of healthcare facilities and professionals in
the HFR and HPR, respectively, in the financial Year 2024- 25 (from 1st April 2024 to 17th
March 2025) is at Annexure-A.
The digital health incentive scheme (DHIS) was launched from 1st January 2023 for
promoting digitization of healthcare and encouraging adoption of ABDM. Under the DHIS,
financial incentives are being provided to healthcare facilities and health technology
companies. As on March 17, 2025, a total of Rs. 73,28,18,430 has been disbursed as financial
incentives under the DHIS.

As on 17th March 2025, more than 1.84 crore beneficiaries have been registered and 9.47 crore
vaccine doses have been recorded on U-WIN since its launch.
The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) has been launched by the Government of
India for promoting digitization of healthcare and creating an open interoperable digital health
ecosystem for the country. It aims to do so by prescribing common health data standards and
developing core modules such as registry of citizens, health facilities, healthcare professionals
etc required for interoperability; so that various digital health systems can interact with each
other by enabling seamless sharing of data across various healthcare providers who may be
using different digital health systems.
‘Privacy by design’ is one of the key guiding principles of ABDM and is implemented
following the principles of federated digital architecture. Hence, there is no centralised
repository of health records. ABDM facilitates secure data exchange between the intended
stakeholders on ABDM network after the patient’s consent. Through ABDM enabled
applications, patients will also be able to securely store their digital health records on their
devices, securely access their records online, and securely share their health records with
healthcare providers after their consent. The information technology Act 2000 along with
policies and guidelines including but not limited to health data management policy, sandbox
guidelines etc. published by ABDM from time to time lay down the regulatory and policy
framework for the regulation of ABDM.

LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3520 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21.03.2025 
 
ROLE OF NGOS IN WOMEN EMPOWERMENT 
 
†3520. SHRI DAROGA PRASAD SAROJ : 
  
Will the Minister of Women and Child Development be pleased to state: 
  
(a)   the details of the schemes being implemented for women empowerment and 
child development through Non -Govermental Organisations (NGOs) in Uttar 
Pradesh, district -wise including the parliamentary constituency of Lalganj 
district Azamgarh;  
(b)  whether it has come to light that some NGOs working in the said State have 
misappropriated the funds allocated to them for implementing Government 
sponsored schemes;  
(c)   if so, the number of cases reported in this regard during the last five years; and  
(d)   the details of the measures taken/to be taken to strengthen the role of NGOs in 
promoting the women and children welfare in rural and tribal areas of Uttar 
Pradesh? 
  
ANSWER 
  
 MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR) 
  
(a) to (d) : The Ministry of Women and Child Development implements various 
schemes and programmes for women empowerment and child development under its 
umbrella Missions namely ‘Mission Shakti’, ‘Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 
2.0 (Mission Poshan 2.0)’ and ‘Mission Vatsalya’. 
  

      Under the Schemes, funds are released to the States/ UTs with the prescribed 
funding pattern for a Centrally Sponsored Scheme as per their respective ratio through 
Public Financial Management System (PFMS) Portal on completion of the requisite 
requirements such as submission of Utilization Certificate (UC), Statement of 
Expenditure (SoE), fulfilment of SNA norms etc. 
  
        The States/ UTs are responsible for implementation of the schemes as per 
guidelines and funds are disbursed by the State/ UT to the Implementing Agencies 
from the funds available in the SNA account which has both Central and State share. 
  
   During the last five years, no case has been reported for misappropriation of funds 
allocated under the schemes. However, under erstwhile Rajeev Gandhi National 
Creche Scheme (RGNCS) discontinued w.e.f. 31.012.2016, a complaint regarding 
irregularities in management of creches was reported against a voluntary organization. 
Thereafter, an FIR No. 39/2019 dated 08.04.2019 has been lodged by the Ministry.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3521
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21.03.2025
SHORTAGE OF STAFF IN PUBLIC HOSPITALS
3521: MS. PRANITI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has issued guidelines regarding the minimum staff-patient ratio in
public hospitals;
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether the Government has taken steps to address the shortage of healthcare workers in
government hospitals by filling vacancies;
(d) if so, the details thereof including the timeline fixed for filling these vacancies and if not, the
reasons therefor; and
(e) the strategies being employed to mitigate the impact of shortage of staff on patient care?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) & (b) The Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) have been developed by MoHFW for
primary and secondary healthcare facilities which provides a set of uniform standards envisaged
to improve the quality of health care delivery in the country. These standards also specify the
required Human Resources, including doctors at various facility levels to meet the health needs
of the citizens. The IPHS was last updated in 2022 and are available in public domain at the
following Uniform Resource locator (URL):
http://nrhm.gov.in/nhm/nrhm/guidelines/indian-public-health-standards.html
(c) to (e) The primary responsibility of strengthening public healthcare system, including filling
up of the vacancies in Government Hospitals lies with the respective State/UT Governments. The
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare provides technical and financial support to the States/UTs
to strengthen the public healthcare system in rural areas based on the proposals received in the
form of Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) under National Health Mission. Government of
India provides approval for the proposal in the form of Record of Proceedings (RoPs) as per
norms & available resources. States/ UTs to ensure availability of HR by creating adequate

number of regular posts as per the Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) in the long run and
using NHM posts in the short to medium term to fill critical gaps. The NHM supplements the
regular human resources by filling up the gaps in human resources in secondary and primary care
facilities (District Hospital and below) as per IPHS.
Under NHM, following types of incentives and honorarium are provided for encouraging
doctors and paramedics to practice in rural and remote areas of the country to mitigate the impact
of shortage of staff on patient care:
 Hard area allowance to specialist doctors for serving in rural and remote areas and for
their residential quarters so that they find it attractive to serve in public health facilities in
such areas.
 Honorarium to Gynecologists/ Emergency Obstetric Care (EmOC) trained, Pediatricians
& Anesthetist/ Life Saving Anaesthesia Skills (LSAS) trained doctors is also provided to
increase availability of specialists for conducting Cesarean Sections in rural & remote area.
 Incentives like special incentives for doctors, incentive for Auxiliary Nurse and
Midwife (ANM) for ensuring timely Antenatal Checkup (ANC) checkup and
recording, incentives for conducting Adolescent Reproductive and Sexual Health
activities.
 States are also allowed to offer negotiable salary to attract specialist including flexibility
in strategies such as “You Quote We Pay”.
 Non-Monetary incentives such as preferential admission in post graduate courses for staff
serving in difficult areas and improving accommodation arrangement in rural areas have
also been introduced under NHM.
 Multi-skilling of doctors is supported under NHM to overcome the shortage of specialists.
Skill upgradation of existing HR is another major strategy under NRHM for achieving
improvement in health outcomes.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3523
TO BE ANSWERED ON 21st MARCH, 2025
EXPANSION OF PM-ABHIM PROGRAMME
3523. SHRI KRISHNA PRASAD TENNETI:
Will be MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the status of implementation of target set for Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness
Centres (AB-HWCs) in rural areas, Block Public Health Units (BPHUs), Critical Care Hospital
Blocks and Integrated district Public Health Laboratories (IPHL) being run as part of the
Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure (PM-ABHIM); and
(b) whether there is any plan to extend the said programme beyond high focus States to other
backward areas including Bapatla in Andhra Pradesh and if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTEROFST A TEINTHEHEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) and (b) Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) is
a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) with some Central Sector Components (CS) which has an
outlay of Rs. 64,180 Crores for the scheme period (2021-22 to 2025-26).
The scheme envisages a new generation of reforms to integrate and strengthen health service
delivery and public health action. The measures under the scheme are aimed at strengthening
health systems and institutions in order to provide a continuum of care at all levels, namely
primary, secondary, and tertiary, as well as preparing health systems to respond effectively to
current and future pandemics and disasters.
Under the CSS components of the scheme, following are the five activities where support is
provisioned to the State/UTs during the scheme period (2021-2026):
 Construction of 17,788 Building less Sub-Centres as Ayushman Bharat- Health &
Wellness centres, now known as AyushmanArogya Mandir (AAM)
 Establishment of 11,024 Health & wellness Centres, now AAM in Urban areas
with a focus on slum and slum like areas are envisioned

 Establishment of 3382 Block Public Health Units (BPHUs) at the block level,
 Establishment of 730 District Integrated Public Health Labs in the country, wherein
each district will have one such lab.
 Establishing 602 Critical Care Hospital Blocks (CCBs) in all districts with population
more than 5 lakhs.
PM-ABHIM is an infrastructural development scheme for strengthening of Public Health
Facilities to be implemented in the States/UTs by respective Governments. At present, the focus
is on construction of health facilities, the work for floating the tenders, finalization of the tender,
awarding of work is carried out by the States/UT government for execution of civil works
approved under the scheme.
For FY 2021-22 to 2024-25, approvals have been given for 9594 Buildingless AAM (Sub-
Centers - Health & wellness Centers) for Rs. 4624.01 crore, 3051 Urban-AAMs (HWCs) for Rs.
2013.55 crore, 1324 Block Public Health Units (BPHUs) for Rs. 1300.18 crore, 504 Integrated
Public Health Labs (IPHLs) for Rs.898.56 crore and 395 Critical Care Hospital Blocks (CCBs)
for Rs. 11614.71 crore. Thus, administrative approvals have been accorded to States/UTs for
FY 2021-22 to 2024-25 for an amount of Rs 20451.31 Crore.
PM-ABHIM scheme is also implemented beyond the high focus states, including state of
Andhra Pradesh and administrative approvals have been accorded to Andhra Pradesh for five
years (i.e. FY 2021-22, 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 & 2025-26) for an amount of Rs 1271.80
Crore for construction/ strengthening of 1786 Building less-AAM (Sub-Centers - Health &
wellness Centers), 45 U-AAMs (HWCs), 26 IPHLs and 24 CCBs, as per proposal of the State.
